problem: This segment is 14.3% of patients but 57.8% of billing value. It generates 1,624 thirty-day readmissions (27.2% of its patients), 1.32 admissions per OPD visit and 97,547 bed-days. Discharge follow-up is not currently structured.
intervention: Post-discharge bundle for every admitted patient in this segment: guaranteed 7-day review appointment booked before discharge, 48-hour nurse call, medication reconciliation, and a named care coordinator who owns the readmission flag.
implementation: (1) Model flags admitted patients in this segment daily to the ward desk. (2) Booking clerk reserves the 7-day slot at discharge. (3) Nurse makes the 48-hour call against a scripted checklist. (4) Coordinator reviews every readmission within 7 days against avoidability criteria. (5) Monthly readmission governance review per site.
resources: 3 care coordinators, pharmacy reconciliation time, protected follow-up slots, readmission dashboard, 1 quality analyst (part-time).
benefit_units: 243 avoidable readmissions prevented; 5,971 guaranteed review visits
kpi: 30-day readmission rate for this segment; 7-day review completion; 48-hour call completion; ALOS
timeline: Design month 1; pilot at two sites months 2-3; network rollout month 4
confidence: Medium - 15% readmission avoidability is the governing assumption; validate on the pilot before network-wide funding.

problem: 22,611 patients (54.0% of the base) average 1.54 visits and INR 2,354 each, contributing only 3.1% of billing value. 16,993 never returned after their first visit; 11,099 have been inactive for over a year and mean recency is 470 days.
intervention: Population reactivation and preventive screening programme: SMS/IVR invite for a bundled screening panel (BP, HbA1c, lipids, ECG) at community camps across the four sites, with teleconsult fallback and a review appointment booked at the point of screening.
implementation: (1) Filter to consented patients inactive >365 days. (2) Two reminder waves before each camp. (3) Staff camps with 1 physician, 2 nurses and 1 registration clerk. (4) Book every abnormal result into a 14-day review. (5) Measure attendance, reactivation and downstream visits at 90 days.
resources: Camp team, screening consumables, SMS/IVR gateway, registration desk, lab capacity on camp days, transport tie-up for the peri-urban site.
kpi: Camp attendance per 1,000 invited; 90-day reactivation rate; downstream OPD visits per reactivated patient; abnormal-result review completion
timeline: Wave 1 month 2; wave 2 month 4; steady state by month 7
confidence: Medium-low - the 7% reactivation rate governs the case; stage-gate wave 2 on the wave-1 result. Non-financial benefit (earlier detection of undiagnosed chronic disease) is real but is not monetised here.

problem: This segment orders 0.64 laboratory tests per visit and visits 3.6 departments on average. 1,917 patients exceed one test per visit, which is consistent with repeat ordering without a standing protocol. Revenue per visit is INR 852 - the OPD demand is real, the diagnostics process is not controlled.
intervention: Diagnostics stewardship and chronic-care packaging: approved order sets by diagnosis with defined re-test intervals, duplicate-order alerts in the LIS, and a bundled chronic package (consult + panel + review) for the remaining patients.
implementation: (1) Agree order sets with clinical leads by chronic condition. (2) Configure LIS duplicate-order alerts at 30/90 days by test. (3) Build the package in billing and the patient app. (4) Audit 200 records at 90 days for over- and under-testing. (5) Report order-set compliance per department monthly.
resources: Clinical governance time, LIS configuration, billing catalogue change, 1 part-time quality analyst.
benefit_units: 421 avoidable test episodes removed, 1,700 package conversions
kpi: Tests per visit; share of orders matching an approved set; 30-day duplicate-order rate; package attach rate
timeline: Order sets months 1-2; LIS rules month 3; clinical audit month 6
confidence: Medium - savings accrue partly to patients and payers, not only the hospital; clinical buy-in is the binding constraint, not capital.

problem: 13,565 patients account for 165,165 bed-days at an ALOS of 5.06 days, and 2,213 thirty-day readmissions were observed. Discharge planning is not segment-aware, so the highest-risk cohort is managed identically to the lowest.
intervention: Segment-aware discharge and ALOS management: risk-flagged daily discharge list, 48-hour post-discharge call for the high-acuity cohort, medication reconciliation at discharge, and a 7-day follow-up slot booked before discharge.
implementation: (1) Publish the daily risk-flagged discharge list from the model. (2) Assign a discharge coordinator per site. (3) Script the 48-hour call. (4) Guarantee the 7-day review slot. (5) Audit avoidable readmissions monthly against agreed criteria.
resources: 4 discharge coordinators (one per site), IT flagging integration, pharmacy reconciliation time, protected follow-up slots, training.
benefit_units: 9,910 bed-days released (3,964 monetised at a 40% backfill rate), 221 avoidable readmissions avoided
kpi: ALOS by department; % discharges with a completed 48-hour call; 30-day readmission rate
timeline: Pilot at two sites months 1-3; network rollout months 4-6
confidence: Medium - the 6% bed-day and 10% readmission assumptions need pilot validation.
